assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 as an incretin hormone and its conversion into long-acting agonists has transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. It is a clear chain from physiology to widely used drugs, with large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion), Drucker (physiology, intestinotropic and therapeutic actions) and Mojsov (peptide identification/synthesis) are the most defensible three. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is a strong fourth name, so the three-person limit forces a difficult exclusion; as I recall it, Habener's role is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Efficacy confirmed in many independent large trials and in routine clinical use for over a decade; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between hormone discovery, peptide chemistry and drug development is contested and I have not verified priority claims.
Long-term safety and outcome data for obesity indications are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of cell-free fetal DNA in maternal plasma opened noninvasive prenatal testing and wider liquid-biopsy diagnostics. The concept is original, simple and has changed clinical practice worldwide, replacing invasive procedures in many pregnancies.
assessment.attribution: A single decisive contributor is credited, which gives a clean one-person configuration. Sequencing-technology enablers are separate and need not be recognized here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and implemented globally for more than a decade; the principle is stable and timely.
uncertainties: Others contributed to implementation and commercial platforms; I have not verified the extent of any competing credit.
Screening performance limits (false positives, placental mosaicism) are practical rather than conceptual.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that raise functional SMN from SMN2 led to nusinersen, a disease-modifying therapy for a previously fatal childhood disease. It is a mechanistic insight turned into a model for RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) form a coherent pair. Contributions of other SMN2 and clinical groups are not in the credited list and are not assessed.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy established, approved since 2016 and long-term follow-up supports durable benefit; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight of splicing-mechanism work versus chemistry/clinical development should be checked.
Gene-therapy alternatives for SMA may affect how the field frames the achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produce durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and have created a new therapeutic modality, now extending to autoimmunity. The impact is substantial and the concept distinct.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain are tied to the construction and clinical validation of CD19 CAR-T with costimulatory domains. Rosenberg is credited for adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other pioneers (e.g. Eshhar, outside the supplied credit) cannot be considered, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up; solid confirmation, though toxicity and solid-tumour limits remain.
uncertainties: Priority among early CAR designers is disputed and not fully verified by me.
Solid-tumour efficacy and long-term safety remain unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, with population data now showing strongly reduced cervical cancer incidence. An outstanding example of prevention of cancer by vaccination.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity at NCI) and Frazer (parallel VLP work with Zhou, deceased and not creditable here) are plausible. Other groups (e.g. Kirnbauer, Rose) are outside the supplied credit; the configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong real-world population-level confirmation across countries; mature and timely.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first made immunogenic VLPs, and the exclusion of a deceased co-inventor, complicate attribution.
I cannot verify details of patent and priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity, and is among the most widely used experimental tools of recent decades. It also has early clinical use in vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth) are distinct steps; six credited names cannot fit into three. Choosing Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, which is a genuine problem.
assessment.maturity: Very widely confirmed as a method; clinical translation is still early, so the medical component is less mature.
uncertainties: Large number of claimants and a methods rather than disease-mechanism contribution.
Allocation across discovery of the opsin versus its application is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is a central controller of cell growth and metabolism, connecting nutrient sensing to growth with relevance to cancer, ageing, immunosuppression and metabolic disease. Foundational and broadly cited.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin in yeast is the key origin; Schreiber (FKBP12-rapamycin) and Sabatini (mammalian mTOR and nutrient sensing) are the other credited contributors. Heitman and others are outside the credit; the configuration is plausible but not certain.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism extensively confirmed; clinical consequences (rapalogs, transplant, oncology) are established though broad ageing claims are not.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would favour the yeast genetics origin or the mammalian pathway work.
Therapeutic payoff beyond transplant and some cancers is modest so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as the repressor of fetal hemoglobin led to the first approved CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, a rare route from human genetic association to curative therapy.
assessment.attribution: Orkin, Sankaran and Bauer are the core laboratory contributors; Thein is credited for human genetics of fetal hemoglobin persistence and is the main exclusion forced by the three-name limit. Allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapy exists, but follow-up is short and the discovery is recent; likely somewhat early for recognition.
uncertainties: Durability, access and long-term safety of gene-edited therapy are unproven.
Compound discovery: genetic association, mechanism and editing therapy may need separate recognition.
